ops.title: A design that overflowed one output block sent two reviewers to review its last 14%
ops.body:
Incident, 2026-07-31/08-01, daemonkit P4.1.

The design agent for the replacement public API returned its deliverable as its final message.
The design was 47,646 characters. One output block captured 6,649 of them — the tail. The workflow
passed that tail to two reviewers as "the design".

Both reviewers reviewed §7 (non-goals) and §8 (decisions/directives) and never saw §3, the entire
exported API surface the pass existed to produce. Both returned substantive verdicts. Neither
noticed it was reviewing 14% of a document, because a tail that begins mid-section still reads as
a coherent document.

Cost: one design pass and two review passes, re-run from a transcript reconstruction.

The rule this forces: a delegated deliverable lands at a caller-chosen disk address, and the
agent final message carries a pointer to it, never the artifact. The final message is a lossy
channel with a silent truncation boundary. Reconcile from the disk record and the lane-scoped
tree diff, never from narration.

Two corollaries measured in the same phase:
- A reviewer given a truncated artifact does not report the truncation. Both here reviewed
  confidently. Do not rely on a downstream agent to notice an upstream loss.
- The same shape recurs at the tool boundary: git apply is atomic, so three rejected generated
  files silently rolled back a 2,358-line merge, and the gates run afterward were on an unmerged
  tree. Check what landed, do not infer it from an exit code you did not read.

Generalizes beyond this repo; the fleet CLAUDE.md rule "Delegated reports are narration — the disk
is the record" is the abstract form. This is the concrete instance that paid for it.
